summary: Round r1 (restricted network). The relocation-fit question is pending. A method is specified: an industry-by-requirement matrix with nine candidate industries and seven requirement categories, to be populated from FDI relocation studies and cost benchmarks. Leads located or reused: NRB FDI survey reports, Department of Industry statistics, WTO TPR 2025 (investment regime, export priorities), ITC post-graduation export-potential study, ILO graduation employment study, Nepal's smooth transition strategy, World Bank LPI, NEA annual reports, UNCTADstat. The web-search budget ran out before UNCTAD World Investment Report files and academic relocation (China+1) studies could be located; these are recorded as data gaps.

findings.claim: Which relocating/diversifying industries (e.g. apparel and made-ups, footwear and travel goods, light electronics assembly, agro-processing, pharmaceuticals, electricity-intensive processing, IT-enabled services) have location requirements Nepal could meet, scored against Nepal's measured labour cost, electricity cost/reliability, logistics lead time, market access and investment regime.
findings.note: Requires `python -m src.cli leads --fetch` for the listed lead URLs, extraction of the named tables and ingest as observations in r2. Relocation studies (UNCTAD World Investment Report, academic China+1 literature) were not located because the search budget was exhausted; cost benchmarks require NEA tariffs, NLFS/minimum-wage data, LPI and competitor data.

findings.claim: Greenfield FDI announcements and actual FDI inflows in manufacturing for Nepal and comparator economies (Bangladesh, Viet Nam, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, India) in recent years.
findings.note: Requires `python -m src.cli leads --fetch` for the listed lead URLs, extraction of the named tables and ingest as observations in r2.
findings.period: calendar year (UNCTAD) / Nepal FY (NRB, DoI) - keep separate

findings.claim: Cost benchmarks: manufacturing wages, industrial electricity tariff, land/industrial-estate rents, and export lead time for Nepal vs comparators.
findings.note: Not yet located except NEA and LPI leads.

findings.claim: Fit assessment scores each candidate industry on requirement categories (labour cost and skills, energy cost and reliability, logistics time and reliability, market access after graduation, input availability, regulatory/FDI regime, scale) as meets / partially meets / does not meet, with each score backed by observations; no score is assigned in r1.

Landlockedness is treated as a binding constraint for bulky, low-value-per-kg and time-sensitive supply-chain segments; high value-to-weight goods, electricity-intensive processing and digitally delivered services are candidate segments to test first, not conclusions.

data_gaps: UNCTAD World Investment Report country fact sheet and annex tables (greenfield FDI by country and industry) not located as files.
Academic and multilateral studies of manufacturing relocation from China/East Asia and the location requirements by industry not located.
Comparator cost benchmarks (wages, electricity, industrial rent) for Bangladesh, Viet Nam, Cambodia, India not located.
Nepal industrial-estate availability and SEZ occupancy (Department of Industry/SEZ Authority) not located.
The session web-search budget was exhausted part-way through r1; further leads for this task must be located in r2 or by the orchestrator.

assumptions.text: Fit assessment scores each candidate industry on requirement categories (labour cost and skills, energy cost and reliability, logistics time and reliability, market access after graduation, input availability, regulatory/FDI regime, scale) as meets / partially meets / does not meet, with each score backed by observations; no score is assigned in r1.

Landlockedness is treated as a binding constraint for bulky, low-value-per-kg and time-sensitive supply-chain segments; high value-to-weight goods, electricity-intensive processing and digitally delivered services are candidate segments to test first, not conclusions.

challenges.text: X33 has no located primary lead; 21C confirms the gap and requests that WIR/greenfield FDI data and a relocation-studies source id be added to the catalog (currently only 'unctadstat' and 'academic').
Relocation-fit outputs should enter goods-export projections only through sector value added and investment, not as direct export-growth multipliers.

uncertainty: Very high. No observations retrieved; relocation literature not yet located; industry requirements vary by firm and period and will be qualitative in part. Fit scores must not be read as forecasts of investment.

relocation_fit_assessment.method: Industry x requirement matrix. Requirements per industry from relocation/FDI literature (UNCTAD WIR, academic studies) and firm-location surveys; Nepal's attributes from observations (wages, NEA tariffs and outage data, LPI/time-release, preference status from 21A, FDI regime from WTO TPR and DoI). Each cell: meets / partial / does not meet / pending with observation ids. Report trade-offs (employment, environment, energy use).
candidate_industries: electricity-intensive processing (e.g. data centres, green hydrogen/ammonia, metals)
